messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing NVMe IOPS floor in ap-south1 after last night's tempdir prune job. ~30 GPU allocs stuck pending, attach latency jumped from ~10ms to 5–60s. Anyone else seeing this?

devin: Looking at dashboards now. scrubber-prune ran at 02:10 UTC. IOPS fell to ~200 avg for ~90s while deletes were spiking; token attach retries visible in provisioner logs.

kai: Correlating node logs: overlayfs flush spam, a bunch of "writeback" WARNs and metadata lock stalls. Saw patterns like: \`overlayfs: lowerdir rename failed\` and heavy vfs -> probably sync/backlog.

anita: deploy history shows canary-cleaner@release/2026-03-20 rolled to 50% in ap-south1 at 01:58. That job increased concurrent deletes per node.

devin: Temporary mitigation: pausing the cleaner rollout to 0% for ap-south1. Running patch now:
```
kubectl -n infra patch deployment/canary-cleaner -p '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}' --context=ap-south1
```

maria: Thanks. Can we also throttle the cleanup? It's spawning 8 delete workers per node which looks like the root cause. Backoff would help.

ryan: Filed INC-30021 to track this and notify customers if provisioning delays persist. Quick workaround docs: reduce cleaner concurrency and limit rm throughput to ~10/s per node.

kai: No FS corruption seen — SMART and checksums OK. This appears to be metadata/noise-induced IOPS starvation and overlayfs locking, not disk errors. Evictions spiked while cleaner was active.

anita: I'll revert the canary in ap-south1 and re-ship a variant with conservative flags: \`--worker-count=2 --delete-rate=10/s --backoff-ms=200\`. ETA ~30m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout for canary-cleaner paused in ap-south1 by anita at 03:12 UTC.

devin: Monitoring — GPU attach backlog dropped from 30 -> 2 over the last 8 minutes after pause. Kernel warnings trending down. I'll keep dashboards on for another hour.

maria: Nice. Follow-up action: add a safety hook to abort cleaner if attach-backlog > 10 for >2m and a regional throttle override. Open to other suggestions. :thumbsup:

ryan: Adding a follow-up RFC in infra backlog to add that safety hook + a canary test that spikes deletes in staging first.

maria: Great, thanks everyone. I'll keep the incident ticket updated with any customer-facing notes.
